data.title: Mediation of IGF-1-induced skeletal myotube hypertrophy by PI(3)K/Akt/mTOR and PI(3)K/Akt/GSK3 pathways
data.authors: Rommel C; Bodine SC; Clarke BA; Rossman R; Nunez L; Stitt TN; Yancopoulos GD; Glass DJ

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Shows IGF-1 drives muscle fiber hypertrophy through Akt, via both the mTOR and GSK3 branches, in cultured myotubes, establishing mTOR as a central node for muscle growth signaling.
data.abstract_excerpt: Skeletal muscle is composed of multinucleated fibres, formed after the differentiation and fusion of myoblast precursors. Skeletal muscle atrophy and hypertrophy refer to changes in the diameter of these pre-existing muscle fibres. The prevention of atrophy would provide an obvious clinical benefit; insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) is a promising anti-atrophy agent because of its ability to promote hypertrophy.
